title: Skip the daily puzzle on a visitor's first visit
summary: New visitors land on the practice page with the daily skyscraper puzzle covering it. This change shows the puzzle from their second visit instead. One change, in brainteaser.js.

steps: Open the homepage as a new visitor (the preview starts with empty storage).
Current: the puzzle covers the practice page until it is solved, skipped or closed.
Proposed: the practice page is usable straight away. Reload (a second visit) and the puzzle appears as before.

hypothesis: For first-time visitors the puzzle overlay sits between landing and the practice questions. Showing it from the second visit may let more new visitors reach a practice question in their first session, without reducing puzzle play among returning visitors.

evidence.statement: 79 sessions from new visitors started on the homepage, where the puzzle overlay appears on the first visit of each day.
evidence.source: GA4 property 546626239 · landing page × new/returning · last 28 days

evidence.statement: 6 of 89 new visitors solved the puzzle and 11 used its 'Skip to Quant Questions' button.
evidence.source: GA4 property 546626239 · brainteaser_played, brainteaser_skipped · last 28 days

evidence.statement: 31 of 89 new visitors viewed at least one practice question; 14 submitted an answer.
evidence.source: GA4 property 546626239 · questions_viewed, question_submitted · last 28 days

evidence.statement: Closing the overlay with the × button, the Escape key or a click outside records no event, and brainteaser_played fires only on a correct solution. What the remaining ~60 new visitors did with the overlay is unknown.
Some new visitors may leave, or lose interest, when a puzzle appears before the content they came for. This has not been measured.

prediction.expectedEffect: A modest increase in the share of first-visit sessions that reach a practice question. No effect size is claimed: the data cannot separate overlay friction from visitors who would have left anyway.
prediction.uncertainty: High. About 89 new visitors per 28 days; detecting a 5-point change in a ~35% rate would take many months in an A/B test, and the ~60 untracked overlay dismissals leave the baseline incomplete.

successMetric.definition: Share of first-visit sessions (a new anon_id) with at least one question_presented event in the same session, from the server event store.
successMetric.measurementPlan: At current traffic, prefer a reviewed rollout with a before/after comparison over 4+ weeks each, reported as observational, or an A/B test via the experiment registry once traffic allows. Tracking how the overlay is closed (×, Escape, outside click) first would complete the baseline.
